_doc: Ar-Ge GDD §4 — the tunable half of the twenty research nodes (§13 calibration surface) plus the hidden lines. The ID / FAMILY / PLACE spine lives in ResearchSeam.NODES as a compile-time const (research_tree.gd says why). ResearchTree validates every row against the seam at load and fails loudly.
_stars: §5.2: the ladder is root 1 star, branch 2 stars, continuation 2+2. A 2-star root would cost a third of the founder's six onboarding points just to open a family. Star N = raw >= 2N (Ürün §12.6).
_cross: §3 — exactly four cross-family links, all on the continuation-B node (the continuation whose parent is branch B). Roots and branches NEVER carry one. §3.1 sapma tavanı is enforced as: the target is in another family, is a root, costs <= 50 effort and no cash — so the worst detour is one cheap research.
_areas: §5.2 — root and branch want the family own area; continuation wants two, its own first. Family to area: capability=product, platform=engineering, practice=qa, design=design.
_hidden_doc: §4.5 — four lines the catalog never shows. Only KENDI KENDINE SERVIS is authored for the demo (§12.1, §13.5): it sits on the test_automation BRANCH so the new-feature-line moment is lived once. The other three keep an empty raw and are NEVER registered — §4.5.2: the node stays visible and startable, its unlock line pre-announces Erken Erisim icerigi so the player knows before spending the effort, it completes normally and its id is recorded in mvp_hidden_lines for a future EA build, but NOTHING enters the catalog and the discovery card does not claim a line opened. Blocking the node would break §3.1 (nothing telegraphed is unreachable); completing it silently empty would be an unwarned loss.
_hidden_k3_doc: The demo line's own K3 must carry a research node and that node must be root-or-branch — ProductLines._validate_step refuses otherwise, and register_runtime_line routes through the same validator. §4.5 names design_system, a ROOT: with semantic_index the top rung would sit four researches deep (root, branch, root, branch), an entire demo run spent on one line.
